mcqs.q: Occlusion is defined as:
opts: The static relationship between the incising and masticating surfaces
The dynamic contact relationship of the teeth in function
The position of the condyles against the articular eminences
The limit of mandibular movement in a given plane
mcqs.explain: Occlusion is static; the dynamic counterpart is articulation.

mcqs.q: Occlusion is described as a relationship between the surfaces of:
opts: The maxillary or mandibular teeth or tooth analogues
The condyle and the articular disk
The denture base and the mucosa
mcqs.explain: The definition includes tooth analogues, so it covers artificial teeth too.

mcqs.q: A fixed partial denture should NOT:
opts: Exert excessive forces on the supporting tissues
Contact the opposing teeth at all
mcqs.explain: It must also not interfere in the inter-cuspal position or in functional movements.

mcqs.q: The design of the masticatory system requires:
opts: A balanced equilibrium of all its parts
Maximum force on the posterior teeth
The condyle to remain out of its fossa
The absence of any tooth contact
mcqs.explain: When one part is overloaded, the strain appears at the joint, the muscles and the teeth.

mcqs.q: In centric relation, the condyles articulate with:
opts: The thinnest avascular portion of their respective disks
The thickest vascular portion of the disks
mcqs.explain: The avascular part is the load-bearing part, which is why the position is comfortable under load.

mcqs.q: In centric relation the condyle-disk complex lies:
opts: Anterosuperior against the shapes of the articular eminences
mcqs.explain: The anterosuperior seat against the eminence is the defining position.

mcqs.q: Centric relation is:
opts: Only recordable when teeth are present
mcqs.explain: That independence is exactly what makes it a usable reference position.

mcqs.q: Centric relation is clinically discernible when the mandible is directed:
mcqs.explain: The clinician guides the mandible up and forward to seat the condyles.

mcqs.q: The movement in centric relation is restricted to:
opts: A purely rotary movement about the transverse horizontal axis
A combination of rotation and translation
mcqs.explain: It is the pure hinge movement about the transverse horizontal axis.

mcqs.q: Centric relation is described as:
opts: Reproducible only with the teeth in contact
mcqs.explain: These three properties are what make it a reliable reference.

mcqs.q: If maximum intercuspation coincides with centric relation, restorative treatment is:
mcqs.explain: There is no discrepancy to resolve before restoring.

mcqs.q: If maximum intercuspation does NOT coincide with centric relation, it is necessary to:
opts: Determine whether corrective occlusal therapy is needed first
Record a new centric relation until they agree
mcqs.explain: The discrepancy is settled before the restorative treatment begins.

mcqs.q: Centric occlusion is defined as:
opts: The occlusion of opposing teeth when the mandible is at centric relation
The position of greatest tooth intercuspation
The relationship of the condyle to the eminence
The limit of lateral mandibular movement
mcqs.explain: It is a tooth contact described at a particular joint position.

mcqs.q: Centric occlusion and maximum intercuspation:
mcqs.explain: Whether they coincide is the clinical question that decides the treatment plan.

mcqs.q: The essential difference between centric relation and centric occlusion is that:
opts: Centric relation is a joint position; centric occlusion is a tooth contact
Centric relation is a tooth contact; centric occlusion is a joint position
They are two names for the same thing
Centric relation applies only to dentures
mcqs.explain: Centric relation ignores the teeth entirely.

mcqs.q: Mandibular movements are limited by:
opts: The TMJs, ligaments, neuromuscular system and the teeth
mcqs.explain: All four anatomic constraints define the limits.

mcqs.q: Border movement is defined as mandibular movement:
opts: At the limit dictated by anatomic structures, viewed in a given plane
Within the envelope, controlled by the muscles
Along the upper border only, where teeth contact
mcqs.explain: The key phrase is the anatomic limit, as seen in a given plane.

mcqs.q: Who was the first to call it border movement?
mcqs.explain: Posselt described it and gave it the name.

mcqs.q: Posselt produced his envelope by tracing a point on the:
opts: Incisal edge of a mandibular incisor
Cusp tip of a maxillary molar
mcqs.explain: The tracing of that single point in space produced the envelope of motion.

mcqs.q: The UPPER extent of Posselt's envelope is a product of:
mcqs.explain: Only the upper border is tooth-determined.

mcqs.q: Movements along all the other borders of the envelope occur:
opts: Without tooth contact, controlled by the TMJ and the muscles
Only when the condyle leaves the fossa
mcqs.explain: They are controlled by the cranio-mandibular articulation and the muscles of mastication.

mcqs.q: The articular disk divides the joint into:
opts: A superior and an inferior joint cavity
A medial and a lateral compartment
An anterior and a posterior recess
mcqs.explain: Translation occurs in the superior cavity and rotation in the inferior.

mcqs.q: Rotation (the hinge movement) occurs in the:
mcqs.explain: Below the disk; gliding happens above it.

mcqs.q: The retrodiscal tissue is:
opts: A continuation of the articular eminence
mcqs.explain: That is why loading it through a misaligned disk produces pain.

mcqs.q: If the disk becomes misaligned, the loading forces are directed through tissue that:
mcqs.explain: The retrodiscal tissue is vascularized and innervated, unlike the disk itself.

mcqs.q: Load testing of the TMJs is important because:
opts: Joints that cannot accept firm loading are not in centric relation
It measures the vertical dimension of occlusion accurately
It records the incisal guidance for the articulator
It determines the Bennett angle on the working side
mcqs.explain: Comfortable acceptance of firm loading is a criterion for the position.

mcqs.q: In the labelled sagittal section, the structure between the fossa and the condyle is the:
mcqs.explain: The disk sits between the two bony members and divides the cavity in two.

mcqs.q: The mandibular fossa is part of which bone?
mcqs.explain: The fossa is the cranial half of the joint; the condylar process is the mandibular half.

mcqs.q: Which muscle attaches to the disk and the condylar neck?
mcqs.explain: The superior head of the lateral pterygoid inserts into the disk and neck.

mcqs.q: Which movement does the inferior lateral pterygoid produce?
opts: Protrusion, pulling the condyle forward down the eminence
Lateral deviation to the same side
mcqs.explain: It draws the condyle anteriorly along the eminence.

mcqs.q: Occlusal harmony is said to matter whenever:
opts: A fixed partial denture is being fabricated
An impression material is being selected
mcqs.explain: The lecture frames occlusal harmony as a requirement of fixed prosthodontic fabrication.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT one of the stated learning outcomes of this lecture?
opts: Fabricate a provisional restoration on a prepared tooth
Define occlusion, centric relation, centric occlusion and border movements
Describe mandibular movements and TMJ anatomy
Explain occlusal schemes and pathogenic occlusion
mcqs.explain: Provisional restorations are a separate lecture; this one is occlusion.

mcqs.q: Centric relation is considered a reliable reference position mainly because it:
opts: Survives loss or alteration of the teeth
Can only be found under anaesthesia
mcqs.explain: Being independent of tooth contact, it persists when the teeth change.

mcqs.q: The transverse horizontal axis is the axis of:
mcqs.explain: Centric relation movement is restricted to rotation about this axis.

mcqs.q: Translation (gliding) of the condyle occurs in the:
mcqs.explain: Above the disk; the inferior cavity is the rotational one.

mcqs.q: The components circled as parts of the masticatory system include:
opts: The temporalis, the masseter, the joint and the teeth
The tongue, the lips and the palate
The maxillary sinus and the nasal floor
mcqs.explain: The system is drawn as muscles, joint and teeth acting together.

saqs.a: OCCLUSION is the static relationship between the incising and the masticating surfaces of the maxillary or mandibular teeth or tooth analogues. CENTRIC RELATION is the maxillo-mandibular relationship in which the condyles articulate with the thinnest avascular portion of their respective disks, with the complex in the anterosuperior position against the shapes of the articular eminences; it is independent of tooth contact, clinically discernible when the mandible is directed superiorly and anteriorly, and restricted to a purely rotary movement about the transverse horizontal axis.

saqs.q: Why is centric relation used as the reference position, and what are its properties?
saqs.a: Centric relation is recordable, repeatable and reproducible, and the position is independent of tooth contact, so it is considered a reliable and reproducible reference position. Because it does not depend on the teeth, it survives their loss or alteration — which is what a restorative dentist needs to build back to.

list: Therefore a reliable and reproducible reference position

ans.text: Because it does not depend on the teeth, centric relation survives their loss or alteration — which is exactly what a restorative dentist needs a reference to build back to.

saqs.q: What is the clinical significance of whether maximum intercuspation coincides with centric relation?
saqs.a: If maximum intercuspation COINCIDES with centric relation, restorative treatment is often straightforward. If it does NOT coincide, it is necessary to determine whether corrective occlusal therapy is needed before restorative treatment.

saqs.q: Distinguish centric relation from centric occlusion.
saqs.a: CENTRIC RELATION is a joint position — the condyles against the thinnest avascular part of their disks, anterosuperior against the eminences — and it is independent of tooth contact. CENTRIC OCCLUSION is the occlusion of opposing teeth when the mandible is at centric relation, and it may or may not coincide with the maximum intercuspation.

saqs.q: Define border movement and describe Posselt's envelope of motion.
saqs.a: Mandibular movements are limited by the TMJs, ligaments, the neuromuscular system and the teeth. BORDER MOVEMENT is mandibular movement at the limit dictated by anatomic structures, as viewed in a given plane; Posselt was the first to call it that. He traced a point on the incisal edge of a mandibular incisor, producing POSSELT'S ENVELOPE OF MOTION. The upper extent of the envelope is a product of tooth contact, while all other borders and movements within it occur without tooth contact and are controlled by the cranio-mandibular articulation (TMJ) and the muscles of mastication.

saqs.q: Describe the sagittal anatomy of the TMJ and the significance of the retrodiscal tissue.
saqs.a: In sagittal section the joint shows the mandibular fossa above, the condylar process below, and the articular disk between them dividing the joint into a superior and an inferior joint cavity — translation occurs above the disk and rotation below it. Behind the disk lies the retrodiscal tissue, with the capsular ligament posteriorly and the superior and inferior lateral pterygoid muscles attaching anteriorly. The retrodiscal tissue is highly vascularized and richly innervated, so if the disk becomes misaligned the loading forces pass through it and it responds with pain or discomfort. This is why load testing of the TMJs matters in determining centric relation — the joints are not in centric relation if they cannot accept firm loading in complete comfort.

saqs.q: Why does occlusion matter when fabricating a fixed partial denture?
saqs.a: Occlusion is a very important aspect for every branch of dentistry. A fixed partial denture should not exert excessive forces on the supporting tissues, nor interfere in the inter-cuspal position or in functional movements. Occlusal harmony must therefore be ensured whenever a fixed partial denture is fabricated. The design of the masticatory system requires a balanced equilibrium of all its parts, so an overloaded part shows strain at the joint, in the muscles and at the teeth.
